title: Prefill coordinator: bounded capture windows and divergent-kernel reconciliation for multi-stream decode
creator: Anika Sharma
description:
Symptom: intermittent wrong-token outputs and rare hangs observed during concurrent prefill+decode workloads on heterogeneous batches. Root cause investigation points to non-deterministic CUDA graph captures when kernel selection differs between prefill and replay due to divergent sequence lengths, mixed-quantization model variants, and heuristic kernel routing. Captures that span long prefill windows are more likely to include stale kernel bindings which produce subtle correctness regressions on replay (observed as skewed logits or OOMs).

Context: existing heuristics attempt to pick a single kernel path at capture-time and rely on replay-time compatibility. This fails when a later event (dynamic padding, kv-cache merging, or quantized dropout) would have chosen a different kernel. The platform currently mitigates by full capture invalidation, which reduces throughput and increases latency under load.

Goal: implement a prefill coordination layer that bounds capture windows and reconciles divergent kernel decisions without full invalidation, improving stability and maintaining high throughput for multi-stream decode workloads.
proposal: Introduce a bounded capture window for prefill: limit CUDA graph capture to a configurable max-prefill-tokens (default 128) and force split-capture if prefill exceeds that window.
Propagate a lightweight kernel-hint vector alongside capture metadata: include selected kernel id, quantization mode, and occupancy estimate so replay can detect divergence early.

Implement a capture reconciler that performs a simulated kernel-path compatibility check at replay time. If divergence is detected, attempt patching using fallback kernel adapters (small wrappers that translate between compatible kernel configs).

Add an epoched prefill token checksum to detect KV mismatch between capture and replay; if checksum differs, fall back to safe re-capture only for affected stream segment instead of global invalidation.
Expose configuration toggles: max_prefill_tokens, enable_kernel_hints, reconcilation_mode (patch | recapture | fallback-to-safe-model), and strictness-level for production vs. canary clusters.
Add unit and integration tests: fuzz harness that randomizes sequence lengths, quant modes, and stream interleavings; perf benchmarks to measure latency and throughput impact.
acceptance_criteria: Replayer can detect kernel selection divergence using kernel-hint metadata in >= 99% of simulated divergence cases in fuzz harness.
When divergence is patchable, reconciler successfully patches and replays without global capture invalidation in >= 95% of trials.

End-to-end throughput for mixed workload (60/40 short/long sequences) degrades by < 4% compared to baseline without reconciliation, while error rate due to capture-induced correctness regressions drops by > 90%.
New config toggles are documented in runtime-operator docs and surfaced in the Console advanced runtime settings.
Automated smoke tests added to CI that validate epoch checksums and fallback paths on PRs touching capture/replay code.
